title: Blueberry Oath
logline: An oath is a key given in public, paid in fruit, with the egg as witness.
epigraph: An oath is a contract that remembers your face.
description: Chapter 7 of Lore.Land: Blueberry Oath. Boof swears a covenant at the ancient market stone. The oath is a key handed over in public; the private price is honest fruit; the egg is the warm, incorruptible witness. Meanwhile, an unauthorized shadow copies the motion without the heat.

content.text: The great market stone stood at the center of the square, its granite top worn smooth and dished by centuries of pressing palms. Boof stopped pretending she was walking alone. For the last three blocks, something had matched her pace stride for stride—a

children.text: that mirrored her four-pawed gait across the cobbles but possessed not an ounce of the egg's honest heat. She set the egg down upon the lip of the stone, scattered a handful of fresh blueberries into the carved circular groove, and understood the dual architecture of the rite: the public half was a key handed over in front of the assembled town; the private half was the honest sweetness of fruit paid into the rock. The witness was the coal-dark cell that kept its own law.

content.text: A stone remembers faces. When you press a berry into granite before your neighbors, you are binding your reputation to something that will outlast your skin.

content.text: The shadow stretched across the sunny cobbles, mimicking Boof's every twitch of ear and lift of paw, but it remained ice-cold to the touch. It was an unauthorized duplicate of a key—motion without permission, outer shape without inner receipt. If you forfeit your public bond or break faith with your pack, the shadow is all that remains of your covenant: the gesture of duty, completely hollowed out.

content.text: "Ah, you’ve noticed your silent companion, haven’t you, Boof?" the Fool whispered from the rafters of an awning. "That is the oath’s shadow—or perhaps the shadow of every promise made with crossed fingers. Anyone can copy the shape of a key, my dear hound. The thief can mimic the turn of the wrist. But whose key is it if it turns in the lock without warming the room?"

img.alt: A cracked market stone, blueberries as the private price, a coal-dark egg, and a long shadow that copies the egg without its heat.

sections.figcaption: The oath-stone: public key, private fruit, one witness.

content.text: The shadow twisted along the curb, occasionally leaping ahead as if trying to lead the dog astray. It seemed to know the exact path Boof sought toward the deep wells in the south, but it stubbornly refused to radiate heat. Boof did not bite at it, and she did not chase it. A key that can be duplicated without an authentic receipt is not a key that should ever be allowed to open a communal door.

She leaned her weight onto the stone, crushing a single large blueberry into the central groove until the purple juice welled up and filled the gold kintsugi cracks. Payment that smelled true. She lifted the egg back into her sling and turned her nose south toward the ancient well that keeps every face without stealing a single soul.

content.text: "The shadow will walk beside you until the journey ends, Boof," the Fool’s voice called out, fading like church chimes across the square. "Because whenever you carry genuine fire, the cold world will try to counterfeit the silhouette. Remember what you forfeit if you lie: the stone remembers faces, but the fruit never lies about being sweet."

loreItems.description: An oath is a key given in public and paid in private. Fruit is the private price; the egg is the witness.
A shadow that copies motion without heat is an unauthorized copy of a key — gesture without receipt.
What you forfeit if you lie is the bond. The stone remembers faces. The fruit does not lie about being fruit.
